stem:
A research scientist is comparing surface antigens X and Y that come from 2 different viruses.  He obtains antibodies from the serum of an animal immunized with purified antigen X.  These antibodies are then attached to assay plates.  Next, a fixed quantity of radiolabeled antigen X is mixed with increasing concentrations of unlabeled antigen Y, and each mixture is added to a separate plate.  After incubation, the plates are washed to remove unbound antigens.  The radioactivity remaining on each plate is plotted as a function of antigen Y concentration, as shown in the graph below.

Which of the following best describes the results of this experiment?​‌​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​​​‌​​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​​​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌

options.label: A
options.text: Antigen X and antigen Y have no epitopes in common

options.label: B
options.text: Antigen X and antigen Y have the same epitopes

options.label: C
options.text: Antigen Y shares most of the epitopes of antigen X

options.label: D
options.text: Antigen Y shares some of the epitopes of antigen X

explanation:
A competitive radioimmunoassay is based on competition between a fixed quantity of radiolabeled antigen and varying quantities of unlabeled antigen for a limited number of antibody binding sites.  Unlabeled antigen that carries the epitopes recognized by the antibodies occupies some of these sites, leaving fewer available for the radiolabeled antigen.  Therefore, after unbound antigen is washed away, the radioactivity remaining (ie, bound radiolabeled antigen) is inversely related to the amount of competing unlabeled antigen.

In this experiment, the radioactivity remaining on the plates represents radiolabeled antigen X bound to the anti-X antibodies; antigen Y is unlabeled and contributes no signal.  Bound radioactivity does not change as antigen Y concentration increases, indicating that antigen Y does not compete with antigen X for antibody binding and therefore lacks the epitopes recognized by these antibodies.  Because antibodies from an immunized animal are polyclonal (ie, directed against many different epitopes of antigen X), the best conclusion is that antigen Y shares no epitopes with antigen X.

(Choices B, C, and D)  If antigen Y shared some, most, or all of the epitopes of antigen X, it would compete with radiolabeled antigen X for antibody binding sites.  Increasing concentrations of antigen Y would therefore decrease measured radioactivity.  If antigen Y shared all epitopes, it would completely displace radiolabeled antigen X at high concentrations, decreasing radioactivity to background levels.  If it shared only some or most epitopes, bound radioactivity would decrease but plateau above background because radiolabeled antigen X could still bind antibodies directed against the unshared epitopes.

Educational objective:In a competitive radioimmunoassay, unlabeled antigen competes with a fixed quantity of radiolabeled antigen for a limited number of antibody binding sites, so bound radioactivity decreases as the concentration of unlabeled antigen increases.  An unlabeled antigen that does not decrease bound radioactivity lacks the epitopes recognized by the antibodies.​‌​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​​​‌​​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​​​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌
